intro: Manufacturing engineers solve problems, monitor operations and analyze systems, skills used across engineering and technology. The closest of the 25 careers below is Industrial Engineering Technologists and Technicians, with an 80% match, and every option needs no extra schooling.
why_it_works: Improving a production line means modeling how parts, people and machines move, then fixing what slows them down. O*NET rates complex problem solving at 4 out of 5 for this job and systems analysis at 3.75. Those strengths match materials science, logistics and aerospace engineering roles. BLS does not publish a separate pay figure for this job, so this page shows each career's median instead of a percent change.
tips: Write up one process you improved, with the time, scrap or cost it saved; it is the best proof for any engineering role.
Materials Scientists are a strong 75% match with a BLS May 2025 median of $117,790.
Add budgeting and team leadership if you want product development management roles.

faq.q: What jobs can former manufacturing engineers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are industrial engineering technologists (80%), Materials Scientists (75%) and mechanical engineering technologists (75%), based on O*NET 31.0. Logistics Engineers are also 71% matched, with a median of $82,320 for their broader BLS group, and they use the same process thinking you apply on a production line.

faq.q: Which jobs for manufacturing engineers pay the most?
faq.a: Among the 25 matches, the highest medians are biofuels product development managers at $171,270, Water Resource Specialists at $167,220 and telecommunications engineering specialists at $134,050, according to BLS May 2025 data. Some of these figures are for a broader BLS group.

faq.q: Do manufacturing engineers need another degree to switch?
faq.a: No. All 25 matches usually need no more education than manufacturing engineers already have. A bachelor's degree is the most common level, held by 62% of workers in a close match, so projects and results count more than new diplomas.

faq.q: What skills should manufacturing engineers build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are coordination, operation and control, managing financial resources and managing people. Operations monitoring already rates 3.88 out of 5 for your job in O*NET, so the gap is leadership and budgets rather than technical depth.
